body_md:
## Fresh developments (last 24-72h)

**AMD Helios launch + Microsoft (July 20 — TODAY)**
AMD officially unveiled its first rack-scale AI system, Helios, packing 72 MI455X GPUs, 31 TB HBM4, and 2.9 ExaFLOP FP4. Microsoft confirmed as a new Azure customer for frontier model inference and Azure AI services, joining Meta, OpenAI, and Oracle. Shipments begin late 2026. AMD stock +~5% on the news.

**Memory stocks rebound (July 20)**
MU +5%, SNDK +6%, WDC +4% as the broad chip complex rallied. July was turbulent: SNDK fell ~36% MTD and MU ~23% MTD on SK Hynix ADR issuance plans (spooking portfolio reallocation) and profit-taking. Fundamentals unchanged — MU Q3 revenue +346% YoY, Q4 guidance $50B midpoint.

**TrendForce 3Q26 DRAM price outlook (July 3–9)**
Server DRAM contract prices forecast +13–18% QoQ in 3Q26, down sharply from +81% in Q1 and ~60% in Q2. US CSP long-term agreements (LTAs) are capping supplier pricing power. Consumer demand weakening at record price levels. Samsung separately seeking +20% hikes on spot/consumer side. Memflation is still positive but clearly decelerating.

**Solar — Section 232 looming August (July 10)**
US assembled module prices held flat at $0.30/W in Q2 (Anza data, July 10). Section 232 polysilicon tariff decision expected early August; Wells Fargo raised FSLR PT to $320 on anticipated favorable ruling. Solar stocks +40% YTD. ENPH drove a short squeeze on solid-state transformer product news. New AD/CVD petition filed June 18 against South Korean modules.

**HIVE BUZZ HPC $220M contract (June 26 — slightly outside 72h window, flagging)**
HIVE's BUZZ subsidiary closed a $220M 3-year sovereign AI GPU deal with Bell Canada and Cohere (2,304 NVIDIA GB200 GPUs). Expected to add ~$70M contracted ARR on top of current $35M ARR. Live late 2026/early 2027.

## Context vs baseline

- **DRAM memflation decelerating on schedule**: 3Q26 at +13–18% vs. +81% Q1. Still positive for MU/SNDK/WDC but the pace is compressing as LTAs cap and consumer demand plateaus at record prices — first real deceleration signal.
- **HBM correction risk not yet triggered**: SK Hynix delayed HBM4 ramp from Q2 to Q3 2026 due to continued HBM3E strength. Late-2026 capacity convergence thesis on track. Micron's HBM4 ramp is on schedule at >11 Gbps.
- **Hyperscaler capex still escalating**: Meta raised 2026 capex guide to $125–145B (from $115–135B). Combined big-4 now ~$725B. No first guide-DOWN visible anywhere.
- **AMD Helios is live**: Baseline expected MI400/Helios in 2H-2026 as a possibility; it delivered July 20 with three major hyperscaler customers confirmed. A competitive rack-scale alternative to NVIDIA's GB200 NVL is now real.

## Most important development

**AMD Helios launch (July 20)** is the standout. This is AMD's first rack-scale AI system shipping to real customers — Microsoft (Azure), Meta, OpenAI, Oracle — with 31 TB HBM4 per rack and TSMC 2nm EPYC CPUs. It validates the diversified-silicon thesis and represents the first credible rack-level threat to NVIDIA's Vera Rubin franchise. AMD +~5%. Second-order implications: HBM4 demand pull (bullish MU/SK Hynix), optical interconnect demand (watch COHR/LITE for rack-scale optical wins), and potential share-shift pressure on NVDA over the medium term. Helios does NOT change NVIDIA's near-term dominance but removes the narrative that AMD can't compete at the rack level.
